1	# How to use ATLAS (the LangGraph-based orchestrator)
     2	
     3	> **Status: planned usage, not yet available.** ATLAS is at the end of Phase 0 (design only). This guide describes how ATLAS will be used according to the approved design. Each step is tagged with the roadmap phase that delivers it, e.g. **[P1]**. Commands and screens may change slightly during implementation, and this guide is updated in the same PR as any such change. Nothing here works until its phase is merged.
     4	
     5	LangGraph is ATLAS's **internal** workflow engine (ADR-001, ADR-006). You never use LangGraph directly; there's nothing to install, configure or pay for. You interact with ATLAS through its local dashboard and a small CLI.
     6	
     7	---
     8	
     9	## 1. One-time setup
    10	
    11	### 1.1 Tools (already present on this Mac, verified 2026-10-22)
    12	| Tool | Why | Check |
    13	|---|---|---|
    14	| Claude Code (`claude`) | Architect, reviewer | `claude --version`; signed in with your Claude subscription |
    15	| OpenAI Codex (`codex`) | Developer, challenger | `codex login status` → "Logged in using ChatGPT" |
    16	| Antigravity (`agy` / IDE) | QA, **run by you** (manual handoff) | `agy models` |
    17	| `git`, `gh` | Repository and GitHub operations | `gh auth status` |
    18	| Python 3.12, `uv`, Node 24 | ATLAS itself | `python3.12 --version` |
    19	| Colima + Docker CLI | Test sandbox (D11) | `colima version` |
    20	
    21	ATLAS never signs in to these tools for you, and never reads their credentials. If one of them logs out, ATLAS pauses that agent and tells you which command to run.
    22	
    23	### 1.2 Install and start ATLAS **[P1]**
    24	```bash
    25	git clone https://github.com/vishnuknehru/atlas-orchestrator.git
    26	cd atlas-orchestrator && uv sync          # exact install steps finalised in Phase 1 / Phase 10
    27	atlas serve                               # starts ATLAS on 127.0.0.1 and opens the dashboard
    28	```
    29	- The dashboard runs only on your machine (`127.0.0.1`), protected by a per-install session token.
    30	- Data lives in `~/.atlas/` (databases, logs, artefacts). Phase 10 adds an optional `launchd` service so ATLAS starts at login.
    31	
    32	### 1.3 GitHub token per project (D3) **[P1 checks, P5 use]**
    33	Store your PAT in the macOS Keychain under ATLAS's name for the project. The `-w` with no value makes `security` prompt for it without echoing:
    34	```bash
    35	security add-generic-password -s "atlas.<project_id>.github" -a "<your-github-user>" -w
    36	```
    37	- Required permissions on that repository:
    38	  - **Contents:** read/write
    39	  - **Pull requests:** read/write
    40	  - **Actions:** read
    41	  - **Checks:** read
    42	  - **Commit statuses:** read
    43	  - **Metadata:** read
    44	  - **Administration:** read
    45	- **Do not grant:** Workflows write, Administration write, Secrets.
    46	- ATLAS probes the token before first use and refuses to fall back to your `gh` login. A missing or weak token gives `BLOCKED(github_credential)`.
    47	- You can check a token yourself at any time with the verification script (it never prints the token).
    48	
    49	### 1.4 Test sandbox (D11) **[P4]**
    50	Tests run only inside Docker containers on a dedicated Colima VM. One-time steps (exact flags confirmed in Phase 4):
    51	1. **Reserve disk space** with a dedicated APFS volume (admin rights needed; find your container ID with `diskutil apfs list`):
    52	   ```bash
    53	   sudo diskutil apfs addVolume <container> APFS AtlasSandbox -reserve 80g -quota 80g
    54	   ```
    55	2. **Start the ATLAS VM** with its data on that volume and **no host folders shared**. ATLAS shows the exact command in the dashboard (Settings → Test sandbox), and refuses to run tests if the VM can see any host folder.
    56	3. **Approve test images.** For each project, choose a pinned image, e.g. `python:3.12@sha256:…`. ATLAS lists the digest; you approve it once.
    57	
    58	If the sandbox isn't ready, projects show `BLOCKED(no_test_sandbox)` with the reason. Nothing runs unsandboxed.
    59	
    60	---
    61	
    62	## 2. Register a project **[P1]**
    63	Dashboard → **Projects → Register repository**:
    64	1. Enter `owner/name`, e.g. `vishnuknehru/my-app`. ATLAS checks access, visibility and default branch.
    65	   - Public repositories: Codex is blocked (D5), so those projects need Claude + Antigravity only.
    66	   - A repository can be registered only once.
    67	2. ATLAS reads branch protection. If it can't, it asks you to declare the required CI checks and approvals; otherwise ATLAS will never merge on that project.
    68	3. Review the **project config**. ATLAS proposes it from what it detects, and you approve it; anything the repository itself suggests is treated as untrusted until you accept it. The file is stored at `~/.atlas/projects/<id>/project.yaml`:
    69	
    70	```yaml
    71	# Illustrative. The schema is finalised in slices 1.3 (config) and Phase 4 (tests); unknown keys are rejected.
    72	project:
    73	  name: my-app
    74	  repository: vishnuknehru/my-app
    75	  base_branch: main
    76	agents:                      # defaults; reviewer must differ from the author (ADR-005)
    77	  architect: claude
    78	  challenger: codex
    79	  developer: codex
    80	  reviewer: claude
    81	  qa: antigravity_manual     # you run Antigravity yourself (ADR-003)
    82	tests:                       # [P4]
    83	  image: python:3.12@sha256:<approved digest>
    84	  setup_command: ["uv", "sync", "--frozen"]
    85	  setup_network: true        # dependency install via allowlist proxy only
    86	  registries: [pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org]
    87	  commands:
    88	    - ["uv", "run", "pytest", "-q"]
    89	  writable_paths: [".venv", ".pytest_cache"]   # must not overlap tracked files
    90	ci:
    91	  required_checks: []        # only needed if ATLAS can't read branch protection
    92	```
    93	
    94	Fixed in this release, and rejected if you try to change them:
    95	- `auto_merge: false` (D6);
    96	- `execution.mode: supervised` (D7);
    97	- no paid API fallback;
    98	- no unsupported integrations.
    99	
   100	---
   101	
   102	## 3. Submit work **[P1 record, P3 planning]**
   103	Dashboard → project → **New task**:
   104	- **Request:** e.g. "Add Google OAuth login".
   105	- **Category:** feature, bug fix, performance, refactor, security, dependencies, UI, tests, investigation or modernisation.
   106	- **Priority** and **acceptance criteria** (each gets an ID that QA must answer).
   107	- **Start.**
   108	
   109	What ATLAS does next, all visible on the task's **Timeline**:
   110	1. **Repository analysis:** stack, tests, CI and conventions. Read-only, by Claude.
   111	2. **Phased plan:** small, independently mergeable phases. Each has an objective, criteria, affected files, tests, risk, rollback and dependencies.
   112	3. **Plan challenge:** Codex attacks the plan, Claude answers every finding, and this repeats up to 3 cycles.
   113	4. **Your approval (D7):** you review the plan, the findings and the answers, then **Approve** or **Request changes**. Nothing is implemented before you approve.
   114	
   115	---
   116	
   117	## 4. Each phase, step by step **[P2–P5]**
   118	The task screen shows the current phase and its state. For each phase:
   119	
   120	| Step | Who | What you see | What you do |
   121	|---|---|---|---|
   122	| Prepare | ATLAS | New branch `atlas/…` in an isolated worktree | — |
   123	| Implement | Codex | Live log; then a **candidate commit** (`r1`) | — |
   124	| Protected-path check | ATLAS | If the change touches CI workflows, secrets, agent config or destructive DB migrations: **approval request** | Approve or reject each violation kind |
   125	| Test | ATLAS (Docker) | Tests **executed** on the candidate, with results | — |
   126	| Code review | Claude | Findings with severity, file, line, evidence | Read. CRITICAL and HIGH block until fixed and re-verified |
   127	| Fix loop | Codex → Claude | New candidate `r2`… Old evidence is marked stale | — (stops after 3 attempts → BLOCKED) |
   128	| QA | **You + Antigravity** | ⏸ **AWAITING_MANUAL** + a handoff packet | See §5 |
   129	| Push + PR | ATLAS | PR link | Optional: review on GitHub |
   130	| CI | GitHub | Required checks on the exact candidate commit | — |
   131	| **Merge** | **You (D6)** | **Approve merge** button, with the evidence summary | Approve, or leave it |
   132	| Merge + verify | ATLAS | Merge confirmed against the candidate commit | — |
   133	| Next phase | ATLAS | Starts when its dependencies are complete | — |
   134	
   135	Evidence labels are shown everywhere:
   136	- **executed:** ATLAS ran it;
   137	- **remote-verified:** read back from GitHub;
   138	- **agent-reported:** an agent said so;
   139	- **manual-imported:** from your Antigravity run;
   140	- **proposed:** suggested but not run.
   141	
   142	Only *executed* and *remote-verified* evidence count for tests, CI and merge.
   143	
   144	---
   145	
   146	## 5. The Antigravity QA step (manual, D4 = wait) **[P4 minimal, P7 full]**
   147	Full runbook: [antigravity-manual-handoff.md](antigravity-manual-handoff.md). In short:
   148	1. A notification and dashboard badge show that QA is waiting. Open the packet: `~/.atlas/handoffs/<project>/<execution>/`.
   149	2. In your terminal, `cd` into the QA worktree named in `packet.json`. Start Antigravity there with a **Gemini** model, in plan mode, using the prepared `PROMPT.md`.
   150	3. Don't edit source files. Ask Antigravity for the final JSON only, and save it as `result.json`.
   151	4. Import it: Dashboard → **Import Antigravity result**, or **[P7]** `atlas handoff import <path>/result.json`.
   152	5. ATLAS validates it:
   153	   - the nonce matches;
   154	   - the candidate is unchanged and the source is unmodified;
   155	   - every acceptance criterion is answered;
   156	   - the model is Gemini;
   157	   - the verdict is consistent.
   158	
   159	   If anything fails, it tells you exactly why.
   160	
   161	ATLAS waits for you indefinitely (D4). Other projects keep running in the meantime.
   162	
   163	---
   164	
   165	## 6. Controls **[P1 basic, P9 complete]**
   166	| Control | Effect |
   167	|---|---|
   168	| **Pause** | Stops new actions safely. Running work is settled, and any queued GitHub merge is withdrawn first |
   169	| **Resume** | Continues from the last checkpoint after re-checking every gate |
   170	| **Cancel** | Stops the task. Open PRs are closed only with your confirmation |
   171	| **Retry** | Re-runs a failed step within its limits |
   172	| **View logs / diff / plan / findings** | Read-only views of the recorded evidence |
   173	| **Approve** | Plans, protected-path changes and merges |
   174	
   175	**After a restart or crash:**
   176	- Everything comes back **paused**, nothing resumes by itself, and the dashboard shows a recovery summary.
   177	- Before you press Resume, ATLAS has already finished several checks: it has stopped leftover processes and containers, saved any half-finished work, and checked GitHub for PRs or merges that happened while it was down.
   178	
   179	---
   180	
   181	## 7. When things stop: what each state means
   182	| State | Meaning | What to do |
   183	|---|---|---|
   184	| `AWAITING_MANUAL` | Antigravity QA is waiting for you | §5 |
   185	| `AWAITING_APPROVAL` | A plan, merge or protected-path change needs you | Approve or reject in the dashboard |
   186	| `PAUSED (capacity)` | An agent hit its subscription limit or logged out | Wait for the limit to reset, or sign in again (`claude`, `codex login`). ATLAS never switches to paid API use |
   187	| `BLOCKED(no_test_sandbox)` | Colima isn't running, host folders are visible, the image isn't approved, or the self-test failed | Follow the message in Settings → Test sandbox |
   188	| `BLOCKED(github_credential)` | PAT missing or under-privileged | §1.3 |
   189	| `BLOCKED(repair_budget_exhausted)` | Fixes failed 3 times | Read the findings and logs; re-plan or cancel |
   190	| `BLOCKED(unsupported_repo_feature)` | Submodules, Git LFS, or unsafe symlinks | Not supported yet |
   191	| `BLOCKED(engine_state_divergence)` | Internal workflow state and records disagree after a crash | Review, then **Rebuild** (audited) |
   192	| `BLOCKED(external_merge_mismatch)` | Someone merged a different commit on GitHub | Review what was merged |
   193	
   194	---
   195	
   196	## 8. When a task finishes **[P9]**
   197	ATLAS produces a **final report** covering:
   198	- every phase, PR and merge commit;
   199	- tests executed;
   200	- findings and how each was resolved;
   201	- QA results and their labels;
   202	- waivers, and anything rolled back.
   203	
   204	It states plainly any step that was manual or not fully autonomous, for example Antigravity QA.
   205	
   206	## 9. What ATLAS will not do
   207	- It won't use API keys or paid API credits, or switch billing.
   208	- It won't read or copy your Claude, Codex, Antigravity or GitHub credentials, and it doesn't use your broad `gh` login.
   209	- It won't launch Antigravity for you.
   210	- It won't merge without your approval (D6), or merge anything other than the reviewed and tested candidate commit.
   211	- It won't push to `main`, force-push protected branches, bypass branch protection, or treat an AI review as a GitHub approval.
   212	- It won't run repository code outside the Docker sandbox.
   213	- It won't send data anywhere except the agent CLIs' own providers and GitHub. LangGraph tracing is off.

1	# ATLAS Architecture
     2	
     3	Status: Phase 0 draft · Date: 2026-10-22 · Owner: Lead architect (Claude Code), challenger: Codex
     4	
     5	## 1. Goals and non-goals
     6	
     7	**Goals**
     8	- Turn a high-level software request into a phased, dependency-ordered plan. Execute it one phase at a time, through gated stages: plan, challenge, implement, test, review, QA, commit, PR, merge, checkpoint.
     9	- Use only official, subscription-authenticated agent interfaces. Never touch provider credentials.
    10	- Survive crashes, restarts and quota exhaustion without duplicating external side effects.
    11	- Isolate projects from each other: repo, config, queue, state, worktrees, agent context.
    12	- Never report an action that did not happen.
    13	
    14	**Non-goals (first release)**
    15	- Hosting ATLAS for other people. ATLAS is a single-user local tool; see ADR-004.
    16	- Running several code-changing phases in one repository at the same time.
    17	- Production deployment. ATLAS stops at "merged + verified CI". Deployment verification is a pluggable, opt-in hook.
    18	- Automating Google Antigravity (ADR-003).
    19	
    20	## 2. Context diagram
    21	
    22	```mermaid
    23	flowchart LR
    24	  user([User]) -->|browser, localhost only| ui[Dashboard\nReact + Vite]
    25	  user -->|manual handoff| agyUser[Antigravity IDE / agy\nrun BY THE USER]
    26	  ui -->|REST + SSE| api[ATLAS Core\nFastAPI process]
    27	  api --> db[(SQLite WAL\n~/.atlas/atlas.db)]
    28	  api --> fs[(Artifact store\n~/.atlas/artifacts)]
    29	  api -->|subprocess argv| claude[claude CLI\nsubscription OAuth]
    30	  api -->|subprocess argv| codex[codex CLI\nChatGPT sign-in]
    31	  api -->|subprocess argv| git[git CLI]
    32	  api -->|subprocess argv| gh[gh CLI]
    33	  gh --> github[(GitHub)]
    34	  git --> wt[(Per-phase worktrees\n~/.atlas/worktrees)]
    35	  agyUser -->|result.json import| api
    36	```
    37	
    38	ATLAS never runs `agy`. The user does, and imports the result (see [antigravity-manual-handoff.md](antigravity-manual-handoff.md)).
    39	
    40	## 3. Process model
    41	
    42	A single Python 3.12 process (`atlas serve`) contains:
    43	
    44	| Component | Responsibility |
    45	|---|---|
    46	| **API layer** (FastAPI) | REST endpoints and SSE event stream for the dashboard. Binds to `127.0.0.1` only and requires a per-install session token. |
    47	| **Workflow engine (LangGraph)** | Runs the task and phase graphs with durable SQLite checkpoints (`~/.atlas/graph.db`, `durability="sync"`), retries, and `interrupt()` pauses for approvals, CI waits and manual handoffs. It holds *where execution is*, never *what is true*. See [ADR-006](adr/ADR-006-langgraph-engine.md). |
    48	| **Orchestrator** | The only component allowed to change workflow state. Graph nodes call it to apply validated FSM transitions inside app-DB transactions, and graph routing functions call the policy engine. Reads gate policy from config, never from agent output. |
    49	| **Scheduler** | Chooses the next runnable phase across projects: priority, dependency satisfaction, repo lock, agent capacity. Default concurrency is one code-changing phase per repo and one global agent invocation per provider. |
    50	| **Supervisor** | asyncio task that spawns and monitors subprocesses: agents, git, gh, test commands. Records PID, process start time, process group, and stdout/stderr artifact files. Enforces timeouts and sends SIGINT → SIGTERM → SIGKILL in that order. |
    51	| **Agent adapters** | One per provider. Build an argv from a vetted template, parse output into typed results, and classify failures into capacity states. Never interpret agent text as instructions to ATLAS. |
    52	| **Capacity manager** | Tracks per-provider state (AVAILABLE, BUSY, RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, UNKNOWN, MANUAL_ONLY). Runs bounded backoff and cheap auth probes. |
    53	| **Repository service** | Clone, fetch, worktree add/remove, branch, diff, commit, reconciliation. Wraps git only; it is not an agent. |
    54	| **GitHub service** | Wraps `gh` for PR, checks, reviews and merge. Every mutating call goes through the outbox (see [recovery-strategy.md](recovery-strategy.md)). |
    55	| **Test runner** | Runs project-configured test commands at the candidate commit, **inside the enforced test sandbox** (security-model.md §5.1; fails closed if unavailable), and captures structured results. These are the *executed* results, distinct from what an agent reports. |
    56	| **Policy engine** | Pure functions. Given the config, the phase and the evidence, it answers questions such as "may we merge?" and "is the reviewer independent?". Fully unit-tested. |
    57	| **Handoff service** | Creates and validates manual-handoff packets: Antigravity, and any step where an agent is unavailable. |
    58	| **Recovery service** | Runs at startup before the scheduler. Reconciles DB state against git, GitHub and processes. |
    59	| **Audit/log** | Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, an append-only `transitions` table and `audit_log` table, and secret redaction. |
    60	
    61	There is no Redis, broker or Postgres. A single process with SQLite is enough at this scale (ADR-002). LangGraph runs in-process as a library (ADR-001, ADR-006). `launchd` keeps it running (Phase 10).
    62	
    63	## 4. Data and directory layout
    64	
    65	```
    66	~/.atlas/
    67	  atlas.db                 # SQLite WAL app DB: the source of truth (global + per-project rows, project_id FK everywhere)
    68	  graph.db                 # LangGraph checkpoints: execution position only (0600, never readable by sandboxes)
    69	  config.yaml              # global config (non-secret)
    70	  projects/<project_id>/
    71	    project.yaml           # project config (copied from user input; repo copy is NOT trusted)
    72	    repo/                  # primary clone (never edited directly; base for worktrees)
    73	  worktrees/<project_id>/<phase_id>/   # developer worktree, one per active phase (agents only; never used for evidence)
    74	  sandboxes/<execution_id>/            # per run: QA verification worktree (wt/) or the extracted, validated /out of a test container (nothing on the host is mounted into the Colima VM)
    75	  snapshots/<execution_id>/            # preserved index/worktree state before any reset
    76	  run/<execution_id>.json              # launcher run files (process discovery)
    77	  artifacts/<sha256>       # content-addressed blobs: prompts, agent output, diffs, logs, test reports
    78	  handoffs/<project_id>/<execution_id>/  # manual handoff packets
    79	  logs/atlas.jsonl
    80	```
    81	
    82	Secrets are kept outside this tree. Phase 1+ stores ATLAS-managed secrets, such as an optional per-project fine-grained GitHub PAT, in the macOS Keychain under the service name `atlas.<project_id>.github`.
    83	
    84	## 5. The delivery pipeline (per phase)
    85	
    86	```mermaid
    87	flowchart LR
    88	  A[Plan approved] --> B[Prepare worktree\nfrom latest base]
    89	  B --> C[Implement\ndeveloper agent]
    90	  C --> K[Candidate commit rN\ndiff guards, ATLAS-made]
    91	  K --> D[Run tests in sandbox\nATLAS-executed on rN]
    92	  D -->|fail| F[Repair loop\n≤ max_repair_attempts]
    93	  F --> K
    94	  D -->|pass| E[Code review\nindependent agent on rN diff]
    95	  E -->|blocking findings| G[Fix → new candidate rN+1\nold evidence stale]
    96	  G --> K
    97	  E -->|clear| Q[QA on rN\nindependent / manual handoff]
    98	  Q -->|fail| G
    99	  Q -->|pass| H[Push rN → PR\noutbox]
   100	  H --> I[CI + required approvals\non rN head]
   101	  I -->|green + authorised| M[Merge\n--match-head-commit rN]
   102	  M --> V[Confirm merge + update base\ncheckpoint]
   103	  V --> N[Next runnable phase]
   104	```
   105	
   106	All evidence is bound to an immutable **candidate commit**, never to uncommitted worktree state. See [workflow-state-machine.md §0](workflow-state-machine.md). Gates are enforced by the policy engine. Any gate that cannot be satisfied because of missing evidence, capacity or a manual step moves the phase to `BLOCKED`, `AWAITING_MANUAL` or `AWAITING_APPROVAL`. The phase never moves forward without that evidence.
   107	
   108	## 6. Evidence model
   109	
   110	Every claim shown in the UI or in a report is labelled with its provenance:
   111	
   112	| Label | Meaning | Example |
   113	|---|---|---|
   114	| `executed` | ATLAS ran it and captured exit code and output | `pytest` run by the test runner |
   115	| `remote_verified` | ATLAS read it back from GitHub | PR merged, `mergeCommit` SHA |
   116	| `agent_reported` | An agent said so (headless run, output parsed) | "I added tests for X" |
   117	| `manual_imported` | Imported from a user-run handoff | Antigravity QA result |
   118	| `proposed` | Suggested but not executed | "Run Playwright test Y" |
   119	
   120	Gates accept only `executed` or `remote_verified` evidence for tests, CI and merge. Review and QA *findings* may be `agent_reported` or `manual_imported`. But a *fix* to a finding is accepted only when an independent reviewer re-checks it and the tests are re-executed.
   121	
   122	## 7. Trust boundaries
   123	
   124	1. **User ↔ ATLAS.** Trusted. Localhost UI with a token.
   125	2. **ATLAS ↔ agent CLIs.** The CLI binaries are trusted as published. Their *output* is untrusted data. Agents run with cwd set to the phase worktree, with a scrubbed env (no `GH_TOKEN`, no ATLAS secrets) and restrictive permission flags.
   126	3. **ATLAS ↔ repository content.** Untrusted. This includes READMEs, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.mcp.json`, issues, CI logs and PR comments. ATLAS policy never comes from repo content (see [security-model.md](security-model.md)).
   127	4. **ATLAS ↔ GitHub.** Authenticated through gh. Mutations are idempotent and reconciled.
   128	5. **Project ↔ project.** Separate rows, worktrees, artifact references and handoff dirs. Agent invocations receive only the current project's worktree.
   129	
   130	## 8. Configuration
   131	
   132	Config is layered: built-in safe defaults → `~/.atlas/config.yaml` → `~/.atlas/projects/<id>/project.yaml` → per-task overrides (only fields marked overridable). A repository may *suggest* config, for example an `atlas.yaml` in the repo. ATLAS shows it as a proposal and applies it only after the user accepts it in the UI, because repo content is untrusted. Schema validation uses Pydantic, and unknown keys are rejected.
   133	
   134	Safe defaults (must hold with an empty config):
   135	
   136	```yaml
   137	execution:  { mode: supervised,   # only value accepted in this release (D7)
   138	              max_active_phases_per_repository: 1, max_review_cycles: 3, max_repair_attempts: 3 }
   139	git:        { use_worktrees: true, create_pull_requests: true, auto_merge: false, merge_strategy: squash }  # auto_merge: true rejected (D6)
   140	quality:    { require_tests: true, require_code_review: true, require_independent_qa: true,
   141	              block_on_critical_findings: true, block_on_high_findings: true }
   142	capacity:   { on_quota_exhausted: pause, allow_agent_substitution: false,
   143	              allow_paid_api_fallback: false, allow_unsupported_integrations: false }
   144	safety:     { allow_direct_main_changes: false, allow_force_push: false, allow_secret_modification: false,
   145	              allow_destructive_database_commands: false, allow_production_deployment: false }
   146	agents:     { architect: claude, challenger: codex, developer: codex, reviewer: claude, qa: antigravity_manual }
   147	```
   148	
   149	`allow_paid_api_fallback` and `allow_unsupported_integrations` cannot be set to `true` in this release. The schema rejects it.
   150	
   151	## 9. Agent role matrix and independence
   152	
   153	The default role assignment follows the brief. The policy engine enforces **ADR-005**:
   154	- The reviewer, challenger and QA agent for an artifact must differ from its author at both the *provider* level and the *model family* level.
   155	- Example: Antigravity running a Claude model may not review Claude-authored work. The declared model is recorded at import.
   156	- If independence cannot be satisfied with the available agents, the step goes to `AWAITING_MANUAL`. It is never silently fulfilled by the author.
   157	
   158	| Role | Default | Allowed fallback (only if `allow_agent_substitution: true`) |
   159	|---|---|---|
   160	| architect / planner | claude | codex |
   161	| plan challenger | codex | claude (only if plan author ≠ claude) |
   162	| developer | codex | claude |
   163	| code reviewer | claude | codex (only if developer ≠ codex) |
   164	| QA | antigravity (manual) | none: wait for the manual handoff (D4) |

1	# Antigravity Manual Handoff — Runbook
     2	
     3	**Why this is manual:** Google Antigravity's terms (§6) forbid using the service "in connection with products not provided by us" and through third-party tools. Google has not said that a local program may invoke `agy` on a consumer AI Pro plan. ATLAS therefore **never launches Antigravity**. You run it yourself and import the result. See [ADR-003](adr/ADR-003-antigravity-manual-handoff.md).
     4	
     5	ATLAS's only role is to prepare an input packet and validate the file you bring back. It does not read Antigravity credentials, watch the Antigravity process, or automate its UI.
     6	
     7	---
     8	
     9	## 1. When you'll be asked
    10	
    11	The handoff happens for any step assigned to `antigravity`. By default that means:
    12	
    13	| Step | Default trigger | Output required |
    14	|---|---|---|
    15	| **QA review** | After code review passes for a phase | `qa_result` |
    16	| **UI verification** | QA steps for phases tagged `ui` | `qa_result` with `ui_checks` |
    17	| **Implementation challenge** (optional) | If configured as a second reviewer | `review_result` |
    18	| **Plan challenge** (optional) | If configured as challenger | `review_result` |
    19	
    20	The dashboard shows the phase as **⏸ AWAITING_MANUAL — Antigravity**. If notifications are enabled, you'll also get a macOS notification (Phase 9).
    21	
    22	Nothing else in that project moves forward while you're away. Other projects keep running.
    23	
    24	## 2. What ATLAS gives you
    25	
    26	The packet is written to:
    27	
    28	```
    29	~/.atlas/handoffs/<project_id>/<execution_id>/
    30	├── README.txt            # these steps, filled in for this packet
    31	├── PROMPT.md             # the full prompt to paste/pipe into Antigravity
    32	├── context/
    33	│   ├── diff.patch        # git diff base...head for the phase

    41	## 3. Merge eligibility (G-CI / G-MERGE-PRE)
    42	
    43	Merging is allowed only if **all** of the following hold:
    44	- PR `state == OPEN`, `isDraft == false`, `headRefOid == current candidate commit SHA`, and the base equals the phase base branch.
    45	- `protection_status` is known (§1.3).
    46	- Every required check from the known policy is **present** and `SUCCESS` on that SHA. A missing required check counts as a failure. Extra non-required checks must not be failing.
    47	- The known review requirement is satisfied: `reviewDecision == APPROVED` when reviews are required.
    48	- `mergeable == MERGEABLE`, and `mergeStateStatus` ∈ {`CLEAN`, `HAS_HOOKS`}.
    49	- ATLAS gates G-TEST, G-REV and G-QA hold for the same candidate, and no blocking finding from any source is open.
    50	- Merge authorisation: a user approval bound to this candidate + policy version and not expired. `auto_merge: true` is **rejected by the config schema in this release** (D6, ATLAS-D11).
    51	- The repo lock is held and no other ATLAS merge op is in flight for this repository.
    52	
    53	**Merge queues and implicit auto-merge (ATLAS-008).** `gh` enqueues on merge-queue branches, and may arm auto-merge when checks are pending. ATLAS handles this as follows:
    54	- It only calls merge when the checks are already green.
    55	- If the result is "queued" or `autoMergeRequest != null`, ATLAS moves to `MERGE_PENDING_REMOTE` and polls. It does not resubmit.
    56	- If the PR gets dequeued, auto-merge is disabled, or the head changes, ATLAS returns to CI_VALIDATION.
    57	- Merge-group CI failures go to FIXING or BLOCKED.

    59	**Authorisation while pending (ATLAS-008 r3).** A queued or armed merge is merely *authorised to proceed*. While in `MERGE_PENDING_REMOTE`, ATLAS re-evaluates G-MERGE-PRE on every poll. If the authorisation lapses, ATLAS moves to `CANCELLING_REMOTE_MERGE` and issues an outbox `cancel_remote_merge` op. Lapses include: the user's merge approval expired or was revoked, policy version changed, new blocking finding, or protection changed. This handles GitHub-side queued or implicitly armed merges.     10	- Every artifact (plan, phase diff, fix) records `author_agent` and `author_model`.
    11	- A reviewer, challenger or QA agent is assigned only if `provider ≠ author provider` **and** `model_family(reviewer_model) ≠ model_family(author_model)`.

    14	  - `gpt-*`, `o*` and Codex defaults → openai;
    15	  - `gemini-*` → google;
    16	  - unknown → `unknown`, which counts as matching the author's family, so independence is not satisfied.

    21	- With the default roles, the developer is Codex (openai), the code reviewer is Claude (anthropic), and QA is Antigravity on a Gemini model (google). That gives three distinct families.
